name: NGC 6362 V40 A
description: The primary star of the eclipsing binary NGC 6362 V40, 0.8337 solar masses and 1.3253 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 5.296 days.

radius.source: Primary radius (solar radii) 1.3253 +/- 0.0077, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)

mass.source: Primary mass (solar masses) 0.8337 +/- 0.0063, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)

temperature.source: Primary log Teff 3.789 +/- 0.009, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K): 6152 K

gravity.source: Primary log g 4.114 +/- 0.005, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)

distance.source: Baumgardt & Vasiliev (2021), MNRAS 505, 5957, Table 2, mean distance of NGC 6362 from 28 determinations: 7.649 (+0.067/-0.066) kpc

text.card: The primary star of NGC 6362 V40, a pair that eclipse each other every 5.296 days.
text.introduction: It has 0.8337 solar masses and 1.3253 solar radii; its partner has 0.7947 and 0.997, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), NGC 6362 V40: Mass, Radius and Period, from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)

notes: Masses, radii and temperatures as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) (https://www.astro.keele.ac.uk/jkt/debcat/) lists them from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K).
SIMBAD knows the system as Cl* NGC 6362 SAW V40 but links no Gaia DR3 source; it is placed at the Gaia DR3 source 0.12 arcsec from SIMBAD's position, G = 18.02 against DEBCat's V = 18.22.

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 5813087468905224320 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 2,000,000 of its distance per century
